summary: As Team Cosmic Variance, we have developed a desktop application that helps researchers and scientists identify and evaluate suitable lunar landing-site options. Our application simplifies the analysis of existing scientific data and performs additional calculations to support more informed mission planning. By combining these capabilities, LunaSight aims to improve the chances of mission success, particularly in the challenging conditions of the Moon’s polar regions.
details:
Project Description – LunaSight

LunaSight is an interactive lunar landing site analysis and mission-planning application developed by Team Cosmic Variance. Our project aims to help researchers, scientists, and future lunar mission planners identify and evaluate promising landing locations on the Moon, with a particular focus on the challenging lunar polar regions.

What does our project do and how does it work?

LunaSight combines scientific lunar datasets, astronomical calculations, and interactive 3D visualization to make lunar exploration more accessible and efficient. Users can explore the Moon's surface, investigate different geographical locations, and evaluate potential landing sites based on important environmental conditions.

The application analyzes several critical factors, including lunar elevation, surface slopes, sunlight availability, and the visibility of Earth. These factors are particularly important for future lunar missions because sufficient sunlight is essential for solar-powered equipment, while a clear line of sight to Earth can support communication with mission control.

By combining these different datasets and calculations, LunaSight helps users understand the advantages and limitations of different landing locations.

What benefits does it have?

One of the main benefits of LunaSight is that it brings complex scientific information together in a single, accessible platform. Instead of having to examine multiple datasets and tools separately, users can explore relevant information through an interactive interface.

This can save researchers time, simplify the evaluation process, and support more informed decisions during the early stages of lunar mission planning. Furthermore, the application is designed to make scientific data understandable not only for professionals but also for students and people interested in space exploration.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Our long-term vision is to contribute to safer, more sustainable, and more efficient lunar exploration. As humanity prepares for a new era of lunar missions, particularly around the Moon's south pole, understanding local environmental conditions becomes increasingly important.

LunaSight aims to support this process by making relevant scientific information easier to interpret and compare. We hope that our project can contribute to future research, educational activities, and the development of more informed lunar exploration strategies.

What tools, programming languages, and technologies did we use?

Our project combines several technologies and scientific data sources, including:

  • Python: Scientific calculations, data processing, and application development.
  • NASA JPL Horizons: Astronomical positioning data for the Sun and Earth.
  • NASA LOLA: Lunar elevation and terrain information.
  • SPICE: Astronomical calculations and reference data for celestial positioning.
  • 3D Visualization Technologies: Interactive exploration of the lunar surface and its geographical features.
  • GitHub: Version control, collaboration, and project development.

How is our project creative?

What makes LunaSight creative is the way it brings astronomy, geography, scientific computing, and interactive visualization together in one application.

Rather than presenting users with disconnected tables and complicated scientific datasets, we transform this information into an interactive lunar exploration experience. Users can explore the Moon as a three-dimensional environment and investigate different locations from a more intuitive perspective.

We also focused on making the application accessible to people without an advanced scientific background. Our goal was not simply to develop another data visualization tool, but to create a platform that makes complex lunar science easier to explore and understand.

What factors did our team consider?

During development, our team considered several important factors:

  • Scientific accuracy: Using established scientific datasets and astronomical calculations.
  • Environmental conditions: Evaluating sunlight, terrain elevation, surface slopes, and Earth visibility.
  • Usability: Making complex information accessible through an intuitive interface.
  • Accessibility: Designing the application for both scientific professionals and non-specialists.
  • Future applicability: Considering the requirements of future lunar exploration missions, particularly those targeting the lunar polar regions.
  • Scalability: Creating a foundation that can be expanded with additional datasets, analytical capabilities, and visualization features.

As Team Cosmic Variance, we believe that the future of space exploration depends not only on reaching new destinations but also on understanding them. With LunaSight, we aim to turn complex lunar data into meaningful insights and help make the next steps in lunar exploration more informed.
